tasks.spec: ROLE: fix worker for the Mott goal-loop Bland pathway derivation (round 6). Work entirely inside your current working directory; never modify, create, or delete any file outside CWD. No network calls, no git, no MCP or Apps, do not load skills. CONTEXT: The goal-loop pathway minted as v101 has a dead data layer. A platform-diff measurement against working production v96 proved the root cause: in Bland CHAT mode the runtime never auto-advances through a silent Default node mid-turn. v101 routes every scheduling turn from the user-wait node n_goal_response through silent Default n_goal_update (userWait false, owns the extractVars) which is supposed to auto-advance to webhook n_goal_search - that transition never happens, current_node_id stays n_goal_response across turns, no variables populate, and the responder invents dates. In v96 the user-wait node n_ask itself owns the scheduling extractVars and has a DIRECT edge to webhook n_search - that is the platform convention. Full grounded evidence: /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mk2-number-and-comeback/workGLD4/platform-diagnosis/DIAGNOSIS.md (read it first). SOURCE MATERIALS (read-only; copy into CWD before editing): /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mk2-number-and-comeback/workGLD3/gl-respond-wiring-fix/ has derive_goalloop.py, build_goalloop.py, check_goalloop_graph.py (assertions 1-5), pathway-goalloop-draft.json (the broken round-5 draft), and fixture-*.json; /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mk2-number-and-comeback/workGLD4/capture-v96/graph.json is the stored production v96 graph - the n_ask node in its .nodes[] is the reference pattern for user-wait extraction (its extractVars) and direct webhook wiring; /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mk2-number-and-comeback/workGLD4/capture-v101/graph.json is the stored broken graph; /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mk2-number-and-comeback/workGLDER/gl-derive-from-working/DERIVATION.md documents the original derivation. THE FIX, precisely: (1) Every route that reached n_goal_search via n_goal_update must reach n_goal_search DIRECTLY. The seven sources currently feeding n_goal_update are: n_goal_response, n_date_conflict, n_date_conflict_retry, n_gate_1, n_gate_2, n_book_1, n_book_2. Webhook sources (n_book_1, n_book_2) may edge straight to the webhook (webhook-to-webhook chains are proven in production verify/book). (2) Every user-wait Default source among them must itself own extractVars covering EVERY variable the n_goal_search request body consumes via {{...}} placeholders except runtime-provided callID, lastUserMessage, and store - concretely: user_verbatim, preference_from, preference_to, day_part, time_after, time_from, time_to, goal_anchor, goal_relation. Follow the production n_ask extraction pattern and keep the goal-persistence semantics (the UPDATE step's interpretation rules move into the extraction/prompt of the user-wait nodes; the persistent-goal spec behavior must survive - the goal fields re-extract each turn with carry-forward wording in the extractor descriptions as the old n_goal_update prompt did). (3) Remove n_goal_update from the graph entirely - no node, no edges. (4) n_goal_search stays byte-preserved from the round-5 draft: url, method, headers, responseData, responsePathways, retry/skip options unchanged; the body keeps its goal_anchor/goal_relation parameterization. NEVER copy any string containing [REDACTED from the capture files into the draft - the round-5 draft already holds the correct real headers; captures are redacted evidence only. (5) Preserve every prior round convention: executable edge conditions (like count == 1), no patient-facing waiting processor, derived-not-generated node content, verbatim slot-variable wiring in patient-facing responses ({{slot_1_day_name}} {{slot_1_start}} etc. filled only from webhook responseData). (6) Extend check_goalloop_graph.py with ASSERTION #6, keeping assertions 1-5 intact: every edge into a Webhook node that produces slot variables must originate from a Webhook node or from a Default node with userWait true whose extractVars cover every body-consumed variable (same exclusions as above); reject any Default node with userWait false on a route into such a webhook; additionally assert n_goal_update is absent. Failure output must be a structured FAIL line containing the words 'assertion 6' (no tracebacks); success must print PASS. Prove it: your validator must PASS your new draft and must FAIL the untouched round-5 draft at /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mk2-number-and-comeback/workGLD3/gl-respond-wiring-fix/pathway-goalloop-draft.json citing assertion 6. (7) Update your copies of derive_goalloop.py (and build_goalloop.py if needed) so the new draft is produced deterministically by rerunning the derivation, and update your copy of fixture-conformant.json so it passes all six assertions; the round-5 draft is the natural red fixture for assertion 6. (8) Write DEBUG.md in CWD documenting round 6: the convention class (Bland chat mode does not auto-advance silent Default nodes; must mention n_goal_update and chat mode), exactly what changed, and the exact command to regenerate pathway-goalloop-draft.json. DELIVERABLES in CWD: derive_goalloop.py, build_goalloop.py if used, check_goalloop_graph.py, pathway-goalloop-draft.json, updated fixtures, DEBUG.md. Do not mint, attach, deploy, or call any API.
tasks.verified: The rewired draft passes its own six-assertion validator, the same validator rejects the round-5 draft citing assertion 6 (watched failing on the exact class it must catch), and an independent structural check confirms direct user-wait-to-webhook wiring with full extractor coverage, byte-preserved webhook config, and no redaction leakage.
